title: Private VPC: chaos-resiliency and upgrade gating matrix for air-gapped environments
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers running Redwood Private in tightly controlled VPCs and air-gapped sites need guarantees that control-plane upgrades and runtime patches will not induce partial failures that lead to data loss or prolonged downtime. This PRD defines acceptance criteria, a gated upgrade matrix tied to observed network capabilities, and a chaos-resiliency test suite that will be required for any Private/VPC upgrade path (online or offline).

Goal: Produce an explicit gating matrix that maps observable environmental signals to allowed upgrade strategies (in-place, canary with staged mirrors, offline physical-media install), define concrete acceptance criteria for each gate, and deliver a repeatable test matrix + playbook for on-call and runbook integration.
scope: Define gating matrix, preflight checks, required operator behaviors during partial connectivity, acceptance criteria for canary/ramp/rollback, and automated chaos tests to validate upgrade safety in representative VPC/airgap topologies. Deliverables: gating matrix doc, test harness blueprints, runbook steps and example CLI/playbook snippets for partners.
out_of_scope: Changes to the image signing pipeline, formal legal compliance audits, and the physical logistics for shipping media to customers. Deep integration with a specific vendor's SD-WAN appliance is out of scope (we will provide generic network tests and guidance).
acceptance_criteria: Preflight: 'bootstrap handshake' completes within 60s when TCP/443 outbound is allowed to the Redwood control-plane mirror endpoints; explicit failure reason returned when DNS or TLS handshake fails.

Operator must detect 'partial-image-availability' (>=1 node cannot fetch image blob) and automatically pause rollouts, mark canary as failed, and surface a single remediation action in Console within 2 minutes.

For air-gapped environments using pre-seeded images, the upgrade path must validate image checksums and provenance locally before applying; checksum mismatch must abort upgrade with actionable remediation steps.

Gating matrix enforced: a site with 'restricted-egress' (only mirror host allowed) can only run staged mirror upgrades or offline media upgrades; in-place network upgrades are disallowed unless preflight network simulation passes.

Rollback safety: any rollout that increases failed pod count by >10% relative to baseline triggers an automatic rollback to previous version within 5 minutes and opens an incident ticket template with diagnostics attached.

Chaos tests: simulated 30s packet loss spikes, split-horizon DNS, and intermittent KMS unavailability must not cause permanent KV cache corruption or loss of trapped in-flight requests beyond configured SLOs.
Runbook: a step-by-step emergency rollback and warm-failover guide must be authored and validated by Solutions Eng during the partner pilot — with sign-off recorded as a Drive link in the ticket.
rollout_plan: 1) Preflight: automated checks (network probes, image checksums, KMS reachability) run in customer staging. 2) Canary: single-zone staged mirror upgrade with continuous health checks for 30m. 3) Ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 100% following successful canary windows. 4) Verify: post-upgrade validation suite (indexing, KV integrity, tail latency) for 2 hours. 5) Remediation: automated rollback and manual runbook if automated mitigation fails.
test_matrix:
Scenarios (each run in sandbox and as part of partner pilot):
- Full egress allowed to Redwood mirrors: verify in-place and staged mirror upgrades. Expected: success.
- Egress restricted to a single mirror host: verify staged-mirror upgrade. Expected: allowed; in-place disallowed.
- Air-gapped with pre-seeded images: verify checksum/provenance validation; simulate corrupted image. Expected: abort and preserve previous state.
- Simulated split-horizon DNS during canary: verify operator pauses and alerts. Expected: pause + no rollout.
- KMS transient failures during upgrade: verify keys are cached for control-plane operations and fail-safe prevents key-rotation mid-upgrade. Expected: upgrade paused until KMS restored or manual override with operator confirmation.
Each scenario must include: failure injection, recovery validation, and post-mortem template filled.
risk_and_mitigation:
Risk: misclassification of network capability could allow an unsafe upgrade to proceed. Mitigation: conservative default (disallow in-place unless all preflights pass), explicit opt-in by SOC contact for any override, and audit log entry for every gate override.
Risk: false positives in 'partial-image-availability' detection. Mitigation: require two independent checks (registry TCP and HTTP ranged-get) before pausing.
Risk: partner-run pilots may have unique topologies not covered. Mitigation: provide an extensible plugin to add topology checks and require customer-run baseline test prior to upgrade window.
